title: Di Resta beats pole-sitter Paffett to win Brands Hatch Race 2
dek: Paul di Resta won Sunday’s DTM race at Brands Hatch for Mercedes-AMG by 1.019 seconds after passing pole-sitter Gary Paffett at the start, with Rast third for Audi after a lap-one safety car.

chapters.title: A home weekend that had already turned on Saturday
text: Saturday had gone to Mercedes, but not to the man chasing the championship. Daniel Juncadella won Race 1 from pole for his first DTM victory, ahead of Augusto Farfus’ BMW and Lucas Auer, and Gary Paffett’s sixth place was enough to stretch his lead over Paul di Resta from 27 to 35 points, 156 to 121.

Di Resta had finished 16th, his first race without a point all season, after qualifying only 12th. Sunday offered the Scot a chance to hit back in front of his home crowd, with a fresh qualifying session to set the grid and a threat of rain in the air.

chapters.title: Paffett goes under 1m18s to lead a Mercedes lockout
text: Paffett took pole position in the second qualifying session with a 1m17.948s, the first lap under 1m18s on the Grand Prix layout. Di Resta had set the early benchmark with a 1m18.021s, quicker than Juncadella’s pole time on Saturday, and was unable to improve on his second run, so Paffett beat him by 0.073 seconds. Paffett said his first run had not been good enough and that he had not expected to be on top until he saw P1 on his dashboard. It was his fourth pole of the season.

Pascal Wehrlein was third, only 0.013 seconds slower than di Resta, which gave Mercedes the first three places on the grid. René Rast was the best of the rest in fourth on 1m18.052s, a little over a tenth off the pace, followed by Auer, Robin Frijns’ Audi and Farfus, with Loïc Duval eighth, Marco Wittmann ninth and Philipp Eng tenth.

Jamie Green, the third Briton on the grid, was 11th, less than four tenths off pole, and Mike Rockenfeller 12th. Juncadella, Saturday’s winner, could do no better than 14th, Edoardo Mortara was 17th and Bruno Spengler’s BMW was last on 1m19.115s, but all but one of the 18 cars were within a second of Paffett.

chapters.title: Di Resta passes Paffett and the safety car comes out
text: Light drizzle fell before the start and rain tyres stood ready on the grid, but the cars lined up on slicks and the heavy rain never arrived. Di Resta got the better launch from second, went round the outside of Paffett at Paddock Hill and Druids and slipped up the inside at Graham Hill Bend to take the lead. Paffett said afterwards that he had left the space for him.

On the opening lap Farfus, Frijns and Auer tangled, with Auer and Frijns running onto the grass, and the safety car was deployed. Farfus’ BMW took front-end damage and would not finish. The field restarted two by two, with di Resta still in front of Paffett, while Wehrlein remained third ahead of Rast.

chapters.title: A gamble on rain leaves Green leading
text: The mandatory stops began straight after the restart, with Wehrlein, Duval, Nico Müller and Wittmann among the first in. Rast stopped on lap six, and a quicker stop than Wehrlein’s put the Audi into a net third. Paffett came in at the end of lap eight, and di Resta a lap later, rejoining ahead of his rival. Mortara’s stop went wrong when his right-rear wheel was not secured, and it dropped him to the back.

A group of drivers stayed out to see whether the rain would come, and Green led the race on the road while he waited. When the weather held he finally stopped around lap 30, which handed the lead back to di Resta. Rejoining, Green got into a fight with Wittmann and forced the BMW onto the grass. He was given a drive-through penalty that dropped him from the points to 15th.

chapters.title: Di Resta holds off Paffett by a second
text: Di Resta crossed the line after 40 laps in 56m23.282s, 1.019 seconds ahead of Paffett, who had stayed within a second of him all race without finding a way past. It was his second win of the season and a Mercedes one-two. Rast, who had reeled in the leaders over the last five minutes, finished third, only 0.357 seconds behind Paffett but unable to pass, in what was his second podium of the year.

Wehrlein was fourth, 11.484 seconds from the winner, and Wittmann the best of the BMWs in fifth, with Rockenfeller sixth after starting 12th and Eng seventh. Auer recovered to eighth, Juncadella was ninth after starting 14th, and Müller took the final point in tenth. Duval lost a points finish to a late puncture and was 16th, two laps down, and Mortara finished 17th, three laps behind. Di Resta also set the fastest lap, a 1m19.943s on lap five.

chapters.title: Paffett keeps a 29-point lead as Mercedes heads for Misano
text: Di Resta said Saturday had been painful after problems in qualifying, and that a single part at the front of his car was changed overnight. Getting ahead of Paffett at the start had been the key to the day, he said, and it gave him the tenth win of his DTM career. Paffett was content with the weekend as a whole, saying the points he scored on Saturday made the difference between him and di Resta. He felt there was a curse on pole position at Brands Hatch, had given di Resta space at the first corner, and had pushed him all race, which wore his tyres. He believed he was slightly quicker but could not make the pass.

Rast said he had not expected the result after finishing Saturday’s race badly, and that he had attacked Paffett once or twice but overtaking was difficult. He also said Wehrlein had pushed him onto the grass twice. Audi motorsport chief Dieter Gass called it a very good podium after the early stop made for a long race, and said Green’s slow stop had led to the fight with Wittmann that cost him many points.

The result trimmed the gap at the top of the standings but did not change the order. After 12 of the 20 races Paffett led on 177 points, with di Resta on 148, 29 behind. Auer and Wittmann were level on 110 in third and fourth, and Mortara and Glock level on 101 in fifth and sixth. Mercedes team chief Ulrich Fritz said the weekend had been another strong one, with a win and a third place on Saturday and a one-two on Sunday, at the home race of both Britons.

The DTM now has a two-week break before the next round at Misano on 24–26 August, the first night races in its history. Both races, the 13th and 14th of the season, are due to start at 22:30 local time. Alex Zanardi is set to make his DTM debut there as a guest driver in a BMW.

facts.v: Paul di Resta won from second on the grid by 1.019 seconds for his tenth DTM victory and his second of the 2018 season.
